D&A PMM Weekly Update · Issue #24

The Future of PMM

July 2026 · Chris O'Hara

This Week

This week we unlock Unit 8: Pricing & Packaging — and I want to start with something that happened last month.

A competitor dropped their per-seat pricing entirely. No more $150/user/month. Instead: usage-based, outcome-linked, pay-for-what-you-deploy.

The sales team panicked. "How do we compete against free trials that never expire?"

But here's what they missed: the competitor wasn't undercutting us. They were repositioning the conversation. They moved from "how many seats do you need?" to "what outcomes do you expect?"

AI doesn't just change what we sell. It changes how we price what we sell.

When your product can do 10x the work with the same headcount, per-seat pricing breaks down. When AI agents handle tasks that used to require human licenses, the value metric shifts. When customers deploy AI features incrementally, they expect pricing that scales the same way.

This week's unit unpacks the new rules: consumption-based models, AI-tier packaging, outcome-linked pricing, and the death of the "enterprise unlimited" deal.

—Chris

📰 News Worth Knowing

1. McKinsey + BCG: The Agentic Workflow Gap

Both firms released reports showing B2B growth leaders are 3x more likely to double AI investment—not because they have better tools, but because they've rebuilt workflows around AI agents. The gap isn't access. It's execution.

2. Salesforce Agentforce Commerce

June/July saw Salesforce's biggest Agentforce update. AI agents now handle merchandising, inventory, and dynamic pricing autonomously. Your pricing strategy may soon be executed by agents, not just informed by them.

3. 85% Increasing AI Spend

New data confirms the investment trend. The question isn't "are you using AI?"—it's "are you using it to rebuild processes, or just to speed up old ones?"

4. KPMG: 75% Expect Enterprise AI Agents in 12 Months

The 2026 Global Tech Report shows three-quarters of enterprises expect to deploy AI agents at scale within the next year. Not pilots—production workloads.

5. Ads on 30% of AI Mode Queries

Google AI Mode is monetizing. Ads appear on nearly a third of commercial queries, and GA4 now tracks AI Assistant traffic separately. The measurement is catching up.
